title: Events and Bubbling
summary: addEventListener, the event object, bubbling, delegation and preventDefault.

steps.title: Listening for events
body: Common events: `click`, `input` (every keystroke in a field), `change`, `submit`, `keydown`, `DOMContentLoaded`. The callback receives an **event object**: `event.target` is the element that was actually clicked, `event.currentTarget` is the one the listener is attached to.
`removeEventListener("click", sameFunction)` detaches it, which is why you keep a reference to the handler.

> **Try it:** open the **Playground**, choose the **HTML/CSS/JS** tab and paste the HTML and script from this card. The live preview runs it in a real browser frame, and the **Tailwind** switch lets you style it with utility classes.

steps.prompt: A listener is attached to a `<button>` that contains an `<svg>` icon. The user clicks the icon. What are `event.target` and `event.currentTarget`?
options: `target` is the svg, `currentTarget` is the button
`target` is the button, `currentTarget` is the svg
steps.explain: `target` is where the click happened; `currentTarget` is where the listener lives. Use `currentTarget` (or `closest`) when you mean the button.

steps.title: Bubbling
body: An event starts at the target and then **bubbles up** through every ancestor, calling their listeners too:
span   ──▶  button  ──▶  li  ──▶  ul  ──▶  body  ──▶  document
(target)       ▲ each ancestor's "click" listeners run, inner to outer
`event.stopPropagation()` stops the bubbling. `event.preventDefault()` cancels the browser's **default action** (following a link, submitting a form) but does not stop bubbling. They are independent.
**Event delegation** uses bubbling on purpose: one listener on the list handles clicks on every item, including items added later.
const li = (e.target as Element).closest("li[data-id]");   // nearest matching ancestor

steps.prompt: A `<button>` inside an `<li>` inside a `<ul>` is clicked. Listeners for `click` are on all three. In what order do they run?
options: in the order they were added
steps.explain: Bubbling goes from the target outward.

items: stop a parent's click listener from running
stop a form from reloading the page on submit

steps.prompt: Arrange the code so one listener on the list toggles whichever item was clicked.
This simulates bubbling with plain objects. What does it print?
code: type Node = { name: string; parent?: Node; onClick?: (e: { stopped: boolean }) => void };
const ul: Node = { name: "ul", onClick: () => console.log("ul") };
const li: Node = { name: "li", parent: ul, onClick: e => { console.log("li"); e.stopped = true; } };
const btn: Node = { name: "button", parent: li, onClick: () => console.log("button") };
for (let n: Node | undefined = target; n && !e.stopped; n = n.parent) n.onClick?.(e);
steps.explain: The first click bubbles from `button` to `li`, which stops it, so `ul` is not reached. The second click starts at `ul` itself.

template: const dojoLi: El = { tag: "li", data: { id: "7" }, parent: dojoUl };
const dojoSpan: El = { tag: "span", parent: dojoLi };

Dojo.eq("from a nested <b> finds the li", "7", closest(dojoB, "li", "id")?.data?.id);

steps.title: Keyboard shortcuts
prompt: Write `shortcut(e)` for a `keydown` handler. `e` has `key: string`, `ctrlKey: boolean`, `shiftKey: boolean`, and `targetTag: string` (the focused element's tag).
starter: type KeyEvent = { key: string; ctrlKey: boolean; shiftKey: boolean; targetTag: string };
solution: type KeyEvent = { key: string; ctrlKey: boolean; shiftKey: boolean; targetTag: string };
